LESSON: READING 7.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.2: Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you obtain the general idea of what a text is about?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a variety of texts for general information and enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 7.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING
This lesson teaches Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading for Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. read a variety of texts for general information and enjoyment
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading above.
2. Explain Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you obtain the general idea of what a text is about?
2. Why is it important to read many books?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. read a variety of texts for general information and enjoyment

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
